AAPL_2016q2.summary_analysis: Apple reported fiscal second-quarter 2016 results on April 26 that amounted to a "double miss" on both EPS and revenue, accompanied by a guidance cut, and marked the first sales decline in the iPhone's history even though iPhone unit sales of 51.2 million came in about 1 million above estimates. For the third quarter, Apple guided revenue to a range of $41 billion to $43 billion with gross margin between 37.5% and 38%, and the board responded by raising the buyback program to $175 billion and increasing the quarterly dividend by 10%. Raymond James analyst Tavis McCourt wrote that the midpoint of that guidance implied iPhone unit shipments around 38 million for the June quarter, down 20% year-over-year, reflecting an estimated 3 million-unit channel inventory reduction. McCourt cut his FY16/FY17 EPS estimates to $8.15/$8.52 from $8.53/$9.00, well below Street estimates of $9.03/$9.95, while maintaining a Market Perform rating and a 12-month price target of $104. He also suggested Apple's June-quarter outlook supported a thesis that the iPhone SE could be cannibalizing sales rather than adding incremental growth, similar to the iPad Mini, though he cautioned it would take several quarters to confirm. McCourt concluded that Apple shares would likely "remain range-bound" until investors see clearer signs of stabilizing revenue growth.
AAPL_2016q2.why_moved: Coverage states shares fell below $100 and were off roughly 5% in after-hours trading immediately following the release, described as a reaction to the "double miss" on results and the accompanying guidance cut. The articles tie this reaction directly to the weak Q2 results, the soft Q3 sales guidance, and analyst skepticism -- exemplified by McCourt's range-bound call -- about whether Apple could return to sustainable revenue growth.
